title: Race on a check-then-act window: limit overrun, double-spend, single-use reuse
index_line: T-0009 · AUTH_DECISION · concurrent bursts beat a non-atomic check · last-byte/h2 sync · corroborated
invariant_violated: The app checks a constraint and acts on it in separate, non-atomic steps; concurrent requests act on the pre-check state.

mechanism.does: attacker issues N concurrent copies of a constrained action (redeem, transfer, verify token, claim)
each request evaluates the validity check against shared state
check compares stale state — no lock spans check and act
multiple requests act on the pre-check state: over-redemption, negative balance, token reuse, duplicate records

sync.window.value: the check→act gap — the target fact to measure

client.burst.value: last-byte sync (HTTP/1.1 hold-final-byte) or single-packet HTTP/2 — defeats network jitter

guard.locking.value: what resists: row locks, unique constraints, transactions, Redis SETNX/DECR

preconditions.expr: operation reachable via a single request the attacker can repeat
usually authenticated user — the interesting ones are one-per-account constraints

success: >1 success among N concurrent attempts (e.g. 15/20 redemptions succeed)
negative balance / duplicate records / counter beyond limit
request timestamps within <10ms of each other
failure_like: DB row locks / unique constraints hold the line
Redis atomic ops (SETNX/DECR) serialize the check-act
false_positive: rate limiter blocked the burst — separate finding, not a race
duplicate successes from client retries with idempotency keys (correct behavior)

hazards: framework-level locking differs (transactions, advisory locks, per-session locks) — inspect guard.locking before spending requests
network proximity dominates: same-DC bursts win, remote jitter loses
non_transfers: queues that serialize the operation by construction
